title.narrative: Lifesaving emergency Food Crisis Response to conflict-affected populations in Sirba and Geneina localities, West Darfur, Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtParalyzed for a year by widespread clashes between opposing parties, resulting in large-scale displacements, Sudan is now on the brink of a famine crisis. All indicators point toward a potentially catastrophic situation, especially in the Darfurs where over 1.2 million children under 5 are suffering from acute malnutrition, with 218,000 of them facing severe acute malnutrition (SAM). West Darfur is among the most affected states, and particularly Geneina and Sirba localities whose populations, already in IPC 4, are likely to slip into IPC 5 if no appropriate action is taken. ltbrgtSI partnered with TGH, TDO and DCD to implement an integrated project aimed at providing life-sustaining support to the most vulnerable households (HHs) to recover their livelihoods and increase their access to food and life-saving services for the treatment and prevention of malnutrition. ltbrgtThe project follows a two-fold area-based programming strategy targeting Sirba and Geneina localities in West Darfur: ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtFood Security and Livelihood support reaching 38,000 direct beneficiaries. ltbrgtUnder this pillar, TGH and TDO aim at providing time-critical certified seeds and tools support. They will provide agricultural assistance (cereal seeds, vegetable seeds, tools training). Recent heavy rains and floods affecting Geneina and its surroundings have destroyed part of the crops, especially those of the HHs cultivating on the wadi banks. In this famine-like hunger context with an expected poor post-harvest season, SI will provide cash for food to the most vulnerable HHs. TDO will help with the treatment of HHs’ livestock animals through mobile-based veterinary service. To strengthen rangeland rehabilitation and improve pasture management, TDO will support nomadic communities with training programs on natural resource management and grass seed propagation techniques. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtNutrition: reaching 10,880 direct beneficiaries ltbrgtDCD and SI will also conduct community-centered nutrition actions targeting HHs with members suffering or at risk of malnutrition. DCD and SI will train and supervise community volunteers to do community level malnutrition screening through Middle Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) measurement and make referrals to relevant nutrition facilities. A solid community network of trained and skilled stakeholders will be set up. Key actors such as Community Health Workers, Community Midwives, Mothers of SAM children, etc., will be trained and supported to ensure, among others, early case identification and referrals. At the same time, DCD volunteers will conduct awareness sessions in communities on good food, nutrition, and disease prevention hygiene practices. Mother Support Groups will be formed in each area to share and promote good Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices. DCD will support 2 Outpatient therapeutic program in Geneina under the project. Following the health facility mapping carried out at the beginning of the project, SI and DCD will make proper referrals and cover the costs of the most vulnerable families. ltbrgtThe project is designed to integrate a strong conflict and gender-sensitive approach. ltbrgtThe provision of integrated FSL and Nutrition activities, and more particularly live-saving livelihood support and Community Management of Acute Malnutrition, in the same affected areas, will contribute to reducing food insecurity related morbidity and mortality. ltbrgtThe Consortium expects to provide assistance to 38,880 vulnerable people. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtMR: During a recent West Darfur sub-national Cash Working Group meeting, co-led by SI and NRC, partners shared updates on ongoing and planned cash interventions.ltbrgtNRC confirmed their active presence in Sirba locality, including areas initially targeted by SI. To avoid duplication and ensure complementarity, SI chose to focus efforts in Geneina locality instead.Security concerns in Sirba, raised by NRC, also supported this decision, as cash activities there could pose risks to both communities and program delivery.ltbrgtlt/pgt
